correctness.rationale: Two independent face tests exhaust all 2^20 subsets and yield exactly 63143 stage-one faces. Deterministic full-Hasse acyclicity checks certify the forward/reverse discrete-Morse matchings and primitive integer attaching maps. Ascending differential ranks 1 and 4 with unit minors yield one free degree-six class; CW attachment classification in dimensions >=5 upgrades this to an integral S6 homotopy type. The stage-zero matching leaves four critical five-cells and the null inclusion follows from pi5(S6)=0. The package verifier recomputes every critical nonstandard premise.

originality.rationale: Two primary full-text sources develop higher-independence and forest filtrations, but their graph-family theorems cover multipartite graphs, whiskered graphs, paths, cycles, rooted trees, cacti, joins, and selected graph products; the 20-vertex dodecahedral first forest complex is not among them. Exact-claim and alias searches of the available record collection and web returned nearby but logically different stage-zero/matching/Cech results. The already known stage-zero dodecahedral homotopy does not entail the first positive stage or its quotient. No exact/dominating counterpart was identified; unindexed duplicate risk remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent unpublished, unindexed, or differently described calculation could have escaped search.
The prior stage-zero result was available only as a published summary; its premise was independently proved in this package.
No independent outside specialist audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A previously determined level-zero wedge of four five-spheres transforms at the first natural forest-filtration stage into a single six-sphere. The exact null inclusion and five-six-sphere cofiber describe the first genuinely new filtration transition on a canonical symmetric 20-vertex Platonic graph. The stage-one complex is eleven-dimensional and nonpure, so the complete integral homotopy classification is informative beyond Euler characteristics or routine face-counting. No larger conjecture is claimed.
